title: Take a Peek Inside the Production Jaguar Type 01
summary: It’s a long way from the wood and leather club room of yesterday’s Jags.
whatHappening: Jaguar is offering a first look inside the production version of its Type 01, moving away from the brand's traditional aesthetic of wood and leather toward a modern design. The reveal showcases how far the British luxury carmaker has evolved in its approach to vehicle interiors.
whoInvolved: Jaguar Cars, the British luxury sports car brand owned by Jaguar Land Rover, is leading this production initiative. The company has historically been known for its classic design language, but is now embracing contemporary manufacturing and design philosophies.
whyMatters: The Type 01's interior represents a significant shift in Jaguar's brand identity, signaling the company's pivot toward modern luxury and likely electric-vehicle aesthetics. This redesign could reshape consumer perceptions of what a Jaguar represents in the current market and influence how legacy automotive brands balance heritage with contemporary expectations.
articleBody:
Jaguar is pulling back the curtain on the production interior of the Type 01, revealing a dramatic departure from the wood-paneled, leather-appointed cabins that have long defined the British marque's identity. According to Car and Driver, the new design strips away the traditional elements associated with classic Jaguar club rooms, replacing them with a forward-looking aesthetic that reflects the brand's evolving vision.

The Type 01 represents more than just a stylistic refresh—it marks a fundamental rethinking of what a Jaguar should be. Where earlier generations emphasized opulence through natural materials and handcrafted details, the production version appears to embrace minimalism and modern manufacturing techniques. This shift aligns with broader industry movements toward sustainability and manufacturing efficiency, though Jaguar's execution appears distinctly its own.

Jaguar Cars, which merged its operations with Land Rover in 2013 to form Jaguar Land Rover, has spent the intervening years reestablishing its position in the luxury automotive market. The Type 01 emerges as a key component of that strategy, offering a vehicle designed for contemporary buyers while still bearing the Jaguar nameplate. The interior design choices suggest the company is targeting a demographic that values innovation and forward-thinking design over nostalgic references to the brand's heritage.

The move away from traditional materials and aesthetics does carry some risk. Jaguar's historical identity is deeply rooted in those very elements—the sense of timeless British luxury that wood and leather have long represented. Abandoning them entirely means the brand must convince existing and potential customers that this new direction represents evolution rather than erasure.

What remains to be seen is how the market responds to this reimagined Jaguar. The Type 01's interior will be the first impression many potential buyers have of this new direction, making its design choices consequential for the brand's future. Early production looks suggest confidence in the concept, but real-world reception will ultimately determine whether this bold departure strengthens or complicates Jaguar's position in the luxury market.

title: Tested: 2026 Toyota RAV4 GR Sport Takes the Compact SUV in a Surprisingly Racy Direction
summary: This souped-up version of the plug-in hybrid RAV4 bravely goes where no other compact SUV dares.
whatHappening: Toyota has introduced a performance-focused version of its 2026 RAV4 plug-in hybrid called the GR Sport, marking an unusually aggressive turn for the compact SUV segment. The new model applies the company's Gazoo Racing (GR) sports and performance technologies to a family-oriented vehicle, bringing track-inspired engineering to mainstream crossover buyers.
whoInvolved: Toyota and its Gazoo Racing division, the automaker's motorsport and performance-development arm, developed the GR Sport variant. The RAV4 itself is Toyota's flagship compact crossover—the best-selling SUV of all time, with over 15 million units sold worldwide as of 2025, and the current best-selling car in the United States.
whyMatters: The GR Sport demonstrates how traditional automakers are blending performance heritage with mass-market vehicles in response to shifting consumer preferences and competition in the SUV market. By applying racing-derived engineering to a plug-in hybrid powertrain, Toyota is testing whether buyers of practical family vehicles also want sportier dynamics, signaling a potential shift in how compact SUVs are positioned and developed.
articleBody:
Toyota's 2026 RAV4 GR Sport represents a bold experiment in the compact SUV market, one that challenges the conventional wisdom that family-focused crossovers must prioritize comfort and practicality over performance. Car and Driver reports that this new variant applies the company's Gazoo Racing performance technologies to a plug-in hybrid powertrain, creating a vehicle that goes where no other competitor in its class has ventured.

The RAV4 has long been the dominant force in its segment. Having sold over 15 million units worldwide as of 2025, it claims the title of best-selling SUV of all time and recently dethroned the Ford F-150 as the best-selling car in the United States after nearly four decades. The model is widely credited with popularizing the compact crossover automobile format itself. Yet despite its massive market presence and proven design, the RAV4 has traditionally occupied the mainstream family vehicle space—reliable, versatile, but not particularly thrilling to drive.

The GR Sport variant changes that calculus by introducing the Gazoo Racing division's motorsport-derived engineering to a production SUV aimed at everyday buyers. Toyota Gazoo Racing, the company's dedicated performance and motorsport arm, has historically focused on competition activities and the development of the GR sub-brand's sports-oriented road cars. Applying that expertise to the RAV4 PHEV suggests Toyota is testing appetite for hybrid performance in the crucial compact crossover segment, where volume and profitability are high but driving engagement has remained largely secondary to utility.

The move reflects broader industry tensions as electrification and hybridization reshape automotive performance. Traditionally, performance vehicles relied on large displacement engines and high horsepower figures. A sportier plug-in hybrid RAV4 must prove that refinement, torque delivery, and chassis tuning can deliver satisfying driving dynamics within the constraints of hybrid systems and the practical expectations of SUV owners.

For Toyota, the GR Sport is a calculated risk—an attempt to expand the RAV4's appeal beyond utility and reliability into emotional engagement, while simultaneously validating the performance potential of hybrid and electrified powertrains. If successful, it could signal permission for other mainstream manufacturers to inject more sporting character into their best-selling crossovers. If it falls flat, it remains an interesting footnote in the brand's portfolio.

title: By 2029, Ford's Entry-Level Model Will Reportedly Be a $25K SUV
summary: At a dealer event last week, Ford showed early mockups of a small SUV that’s slated to start at $25,000 and offer hybrid and nonhybrid powertrains.
whatHappening: Ford is planning to launch a new entry-level SUV by 2029 with a starting price of $25,000. The company displayed early mockups of the vehicle at a dealer event, featuring both hybrid and nonhybrid powertrain options.
whoInvolved: Ford Motor Company, the American multinational automobile manufacturer headquartered in Dearborn, Michigan, is spearheading this initiative. Founded by Henry Ford in 1903 and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker F, the company sells vehicles under the Ford brand as well as luxury cars under its Lincoln brand.
whyMatters: The $25,000 entry-level SUV could reshape Ford's position in the affordable vehicle segment, directly competing with mass-market alternatives as consumer demand for SUVs continues to dominate the market. The inclusion of hybrid options signals Ford's commitment to offering fuel-efficient choices across its lineup, aligning with shifting consumer preferences and regulatory pressures toward electrification.
articleBody:
Ford Motor Company is preparing to introduce a new small SUV positioned at the budget-conscious end of the market, with plans to begin sales by 2029. According to Car and Driver, Ford displayed early mockups of the vehicle at a recent dealer event, revealing a model designed to compete aggressively in the entry-level segment with a starting price of $25,000. The automaker is planning to offer both hybrid and nonhybrid powertrain options, giving buyers flexibility in fuel efficiency and cost.

The announcement represents a significant strategic move for the Dearborn, Michigan-based manufacturer. Ford Motor Company, founded by Henry Ford in 1903, has long maintained a presence across multiple market segments through its Ford brand and its luxury Lincoln division. By introducing an affordable SUV option, the company aims to capture price-sensitive customers who have increasingly gravitated toward SUVs over traditional sedans in recent years.

The timing of this release aligns with Ford's broader strategy to modernize its vehicle lineup and respond to evolving consumer preferences. The inclusion of hybrid powertrains signals that the company is preparing its entry-level offerings to meet growing expectations around fuel economy without requiring customers to move to fully electric vehicles. This dual-powertrain approach allows Ford to appeal to both traditionally minded buyers and those seeking incremental steps toward greener transportation.

The $25,000 price point represents an aggressive positioning that could reshape the competitive landscape for affordable SUVs. At that price level, Ford would be targeting buyers currently considering vehicles from manufacturers known for value-oriented offerings. The early mockups shown at the dealer event suggest the vehicle is still in development, with the multi-year runway until 2029 providing Ford time to refine design, engineering, and manufacturing processes.

The project underscores Ford's commitment to maintaining relevance across all market tiers during a period of significant industry transformation. As automakers navigate electrification mandates and shifting consumer preferences, maintaining a robust entry-level offering has become increasingly important for market share and brand loyalty. Ford's strategy of offering multiple powertrain choices at the affordable end reflects the reality that consumer adoption of electric vehicles remains gradual, and hybrid technology serves as a transitional option for many buyers.

title: Eccentrica V12 Roadster Makes the Diablo Restomod Roofless
summary: Maybe you've never heard of Eccentrica, but you’ve certainly heard of the Lamborghini Diablo the V12 Roadster is based on.
whatHappening: Eccentrica has unveiled a roofless restomod version of the iconic Lamborghini Diablo, transforming the legendary supercar into an open-air V12 roadster. The conversion removes the car's roof while maintaining the mid-engine performance that made the original a benchmark for high-speed supercars.
whoInvolved: Eccentrica, a restomod specialist, has partnered with the Lamborghini Diablo platform—one of the most celebrated supercars ever built by Italian manufacturer Lamborghini. The original Diablo was produced from 1990 to 2001 and holds distinction as the first production Lamborghini to exceed 200 mph.
whyMatters: Restomod projects like this extend the life and appeal of classic supercars by combining vintage design with modern customization, attracting collectors and enthusiasts willing to invest in bespoke conversions. The Diablo's legendary V12 engine and performance credentials make it a prime candidate for high-end restoration work, and removing the roof creates a rare and highly desirable variant.
articleBody:
Eccentrica has unveiled a striking reimagining of one of automotive history's most iconic supercars: a roofless version of the Lamborghini Diablo V12 Roadster. The restomod converts the coupe into an open-air machine while preserving the mid-mounted V12 engine and longitudinal layout that defined the original design.

The Lamborghini Diablo, produced by the Italian manufacturer from 1990 through 2001, was groundbreaking in its era. It was the first production Lamborghini to achieve a top speed exceeding 200 mph, representing a major leap in supercar performance and establishing new benchmarks for the segment. The Diablo's long production run and enduring reputation have made it a favorite subject for restomod specialists seeking to blend classic appeal with modern refinements.

According to Car and Driver, Eccentrica's approach transforms the Diablo into a roadster configuration, removing the fixed roof to create an open cockpit experience. This conversion is particularly ambitious given the structural modifications required to maintain the car's rigidity and safety without roof support. The result is a rare variant that appeals to collectors seeking a unique take on an already legendary machine.

Eccentrica's work represents a broader trend in the automotive customization world, where specialists take classic supercars and reinterpret them for contemporary buyers. By removing the roof from a car originally engineered as a coupe, the company creates a bespoke driving experience that the original manufacturer never offered. The Diablo's robust mid-engine platform and proven performance envelope make it an ideal candidate for such extensive modification.

The restomod market has grown substantially in recent years, driven by wealthy enthusiasts and collectors who value the combination of classic design language and modern engineering. Converting a Diablo—already one of the most sought-after supercars from the 1990s—into a one-off roadster elevates the car's exclusivity and collectibility. For those seeking a visceral, open-air driving experience in a car with authentic supercar credentials, Eccentrica's roofless Diablo represents an increasingly appealing alternative to purchasing a new machine.

title: View Photos of the 2004 Luxury Convertibles
summary: View exterior and interior photos of the 2004 Cadillac XLR, Jaguar XK, Lexus SC430, Mercedes-Benz SLK320, and Porsche 911 Carrera 4 Cabriolet.
whatHappening: Car and Driver has released a photo gallery showcasing five of 2004's premier luxury convertibles, offering viewers a visual tour of the year's most coveted open-air vehicles from leading automotive brands.
whoInvolved: Car and Driver, a major automotive publication, has compiled images of convertibles from Cadillac, Jaguar, Lexus, Mercedes-Benz, and Porsche—five of the world's most prestigious automakers competing in the high-end convertible market.
whyMatters: The 2004 model year represents a significant moment for luxury convertibles, with new entries like the Cadillac XLR launching alongside established rivals. For consumers considering six-figure purchases, visual documentation of exterior styling and interior appointments directly influences buying decisions in this premium segment.
articleBody:
Car and Driver reports on the 2004 luxury convertible market with a comprehensive photo gallery capturing the year's most exclusive open-air vehicles. The selection spans five iconic nameplates—the Cadillac XLR, Jaguar XK, Lexus SC430, Mercedes-Benz SLK320, and Porsche 911 Carrera 4 Cabriolet—each representing the pinnacle of convertible design and engineering from their respective manufacturers.

The Cadillac XLR stands out as a new entrant, having begun production for the 2004 model year following its introduction at the 2003 North American International Auto Show. The two-seat roadster features a power retractable hardtop and was conceived as a halo model for Cadillac, with its design drawing inspiration from the 1999 Evoq concept car. This marks a significant moment for the American luxury brand's return to the high-performance convertible segment.

The other vehicles in the gallery represent well-established players in the luxury convertible category. The Porsche 911 Carrera 4 Cabriolet continues the 911's legacy as a rear-engine sports car, a design lineage stretching back to the model's introduction in September 1964. The 911's core concept has remained largely consistent across generations, though continuous refinement—including the transition from air-cooled to water-cooled engines and modern suspension systems—has kept the model competitive.

For prospective buyers in 2004, the gallery provides essential visual reference points when evaluating vehicles that typically command price tags in the six figures. The mix of exterior styling cues, interior trim materials, and hardtop or soft-top configurations differentiates each offering and allows consumers to compare aesthetic and functional approaches from different design philosophies.

The breadth of the selection reflects the strength of the luxury convertible market in 2004, a year when manufacturers across multiple continents were investing in open-air performance and prestige vehicles. Whether opting for American, British, Japanese, German, or other European design sensibilities, buyers had unprecedented choice among vehicles that combined convertible practicality with luxury appointments and performance capabilities.

title: 2004 Luxury Convertibles Compared: Cadillac's XLR Looks To Disrupt the Topless Status Quo
summary: In the world of stylish $75,000 GT cabriolets, can the new Caddy XLR compete with the big-time glamour boys by Jaguar, Lexus, Mercedes-Benz, and Porsche?
whatHappening: Cadillac is launching its new XLR convertible as a direct challenger to established luxury roadster makers, entering a competitive segment dominated by Jaguar, Lexus, Mercedes-Benz, and Porsche. The 2004 model year vehicle aims to shake up the $75,000 grand touring convertible market with American-made styling and engineering.
whoInvolved: Cadillac, a luxury division of General Motors, is positioning itself against established European and Japanese competitors in the convertible sports car segment. The XLR represents Cadillac's effort to revive its prestige marque through a high-end halo model designed to appeal to affluent consumers seeking premium open-air driving experiences.
whyMatters: Cadillac's entry into the luxury convertible market signals the American automaker's commitment to competing directly with global prestige brands in a historically European-dominated category. The success or failure of the XLR will test whether American design and engineering can capture market share from entrenched competitors like Mercedes-Benz and Porsche among wealthy convertible enthusiasts.
articleBody:
The 2004 model year marks a significant moment for Cadillac as it introduces the XLR convertible, a new entrant into one of the most prestigious automotive categories: the $75,000 luxury grand touring cabriolet. According to Car and Driver, the question facing the industry is whether Cadillac's fresh offering can genuinely compete with the established glamour and cachet of Jaguar, Lexus, Mercedes-Benz, and Porsche in this rarified market segment.

The XLR arrives as a two-seat roadster equipped with a power retractable hardtop, representing a significant engineering commitment from Cadillac. Introduced at the 2003 North American International Auto Show as a halo model for the brand, the XLR began production for this model year following inspiration from the 1999 Evoq concept car. The vehicle's arrival reflects Cadillac's ambition to establish itself not merely as a purveyor of luxury sedans, but as a serious player in the high-performance convertible space where engineering sophistication and design excellence are paramount.

Competing in this segment means facing off against manufacturers with decades or centuries of pedigree in sports car manufacturing. Mercedes-Benz, which has produced the storied SL-Class grand touring sports car since 1954, represents the kind of established heritage that prospective XLR buyers must weigh against Cadillac's proposition. The SL-Class designation itself derives from the German term "Super-Leicht," or "Super Light," reflecting the engineering philosophy that has defined Mercedes' approach to convertible performance for generations. Porsche, Jaguar, and Lexus bring equally compelling brand narratives and proven track records in the luxury convertible category.

For Cadillac, the XLR represents both an opportunity and a considerable challenge. The American luxury brand must convince affluent consumers accustomed to European design language and performance credentials that its vision of the modern convertible merits consideration alongside tradition-laden competitors. The power retractable hardtop technology offers genuine innovation—a feature that distinguishes the XLR from many of its rivals and provides practical advantages in varying weather conditions while maintaining the open-air driving experience that defines the category.

The launch of the XLR in 2004 will test whether American automotive ambition can successfully disrupt a market where European prestige and heritage have long held sway. Success would validate Cadillac's strategy of competing head-to-head with global luxury brands in their most demanding categories. The convertible market, where buyers are typically most style-conscious and least price-sensitive, represents a crucial proving ground for Cadillac's broader efforts to reclaim relevance among the world's most discerning automotive enthusiasts.

articleBody:
