title: 1969 Subaru Sambar 360 Van For Sale on Bring a Trailer
summary: Subaru got its start in America with microcars like this.
whatHappening: A 1969 Subaru Sambar 360 Van is being offered for sale on Bring a Trailer, the online auction platform for collector vehicles. The listing highlights one of the earliest microcars that helped establish Subaru's presence in the American market.
whoInvolved: Subaru, the Japanese automaker that is now the twenty-first largest by production worldwide, is the manufacturer behind this vehicle. Bring a Trailer is the online marketplace facilitating the sale of this collector vehicle.
whyMatters: This sale reflects growing collector interest in forgotten automotive history and Japan's early microcar engineering. The Subaru 360 and its variants represent a crucial chapter in how Japanese manufacturers first penetrated Western markets with affordable, innovative vehicles that defied conventional automotive wisdom of the era.
articleBody:
A 1969 Subaru Sambar 360 Van has appeared on Bring a Trailer, offering collectors a rare chance to own one of the vehicles that launched Subaru's American presence. The Sambar, a commercial variant of the iconic Subaru 360, represents a fascinating footnote in automotive history—a time when Japanese manufacturers challenged American and European dominance with ingenious small-car engineering.

The Subaru 360 itself was the company's first mass-produced automobile, manufactured from 1958 to 1971. Over its 12-year run, production reached 392,000 units, making it a commercial success despite its diminutive size and rear-engine layout. The Sambar van variant extended this platform into the commercial market, offering practicality in a compact footprint ideal for Japan's crowded urban streets and narrow roads. By 1969, when this particular van was built, the 360 had already proven its viability in the Japanese market and was beginning to attract attention from adventurous buyers abroad.

According to Car and Driver, Subaru's entry into America relied heavily on microcars like the 360 and its variants. These vehicles embodied a philosophy radically different from Detroit's prevailing approach: rather than larger engines and more chrome, Japanese manufacturers offered efficiency, reliability, and clever engineering. The Sambar van, with its boxy design and modest proportions, typified this approach—maximizing interior space within a minimal footprint, a principle that would influence vehicle design for decades to come.

The survival of a 1969 Sambar to the collector-car market today is noteworthy. These utilitarian vehicles were built to work, not to be preserved, and many were driven into obscurity or scrapped as they aged. Finding one intact enough for auction speaks to either exceptional care by its previous owners or fortunate circumstances. For Subaru enthusiasts and microcar collectors, such vehicles now represent a tangible connection to the company's humble origins—before it became a major global automaker.

The online auction format of Bring a Trailer has made it easier for specialized vehicles to find interested buyers across the globe. A 1969 Sambar van would have been nearly impossible to sell through traditional channels just years ago, yet today it attracts bidders who recognize the historical and cultural significance of Japan's early automotive exports. This shift in how collector cars are bought and sold has given new life to vehicles that might otherwise have disappeared from public consciousness.

title: Lease Like a 'Car and Driver' Editor
summary: Here's how I get a great lease deal while incurring the least amount of hassle.
whatHappening: A Car and Driver editor shares insider strategies for negotiating favorable vehicle lease deals while minimizing the typical friction and complexity involved in the leasing process. The piece offers practical guidance on securing better terms and streamlining the transaction.
whoInvolved: Car and Driver, the American automotive enthusiast magazine founded in 1955 and currently owned by Hearst Magazines, publishes this advice from one of its editors. Based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, the magazine has long served as a trusted source for automotive expertise and consumer guidance.
whyMatters: Leasing advice from automotive journalists reaches millions of car shoppers facing the decision between purchasing and leasing vehicles. Practical strategies from an industry insider can help consumers navigate a transaction that often involves complex negotiations and hidden costs, potentially saving time and money on one of the largest purchases most people make.
articleBody:
Car and Driver, a leading voice in automotive journalism since its 1955 debut, reports on how one of its editors approaches vehicle leasing to achieve favorable terms with minimal hassle. The strategy reflects the kind of informed, practical approach that has made the magazine a trusted resource for consumers navigating complex automotive decisions.

Vehicle leasing has become an increasingly popular alternative to outright purchase, particularly among consumers who prefer driving new cars with the latest technology and safety features. However, the leasing process often intimidates buyers unfamiliar with industry terminology, dealer tactics, and the various fees and terms that shape the final deal. An experienced automotive journalist possesses unique insight into how dealerships structure these transactions and where opportunities exist to negotiate better conditions.

The editor's approach emphasizes understanding the key variables that determine lease costs and terms. Rather than accepting dealer-proposed numbers at face value, informed lessees research comparable vehicles, know the residual values and depreciation curves, and understand how interest rates and acquisition fees affect monthly payments. By entering negotiations with this knowledge, consumers can identify inflated figures and push back effectively.

Reducing hassle involves streamlining the transaction process itself. This includes preparing all necessary financial documentation beforehand, deciding on a vehicle and lease structure before visiting the dealership, and being willing to walk away if terms prove unsatisfactory. Such disciplined approaches prevent the lengthy back-and-forth negotiations and pressure tactics that make leasing feel burdensome for many consumers.

The guidance also addresses timing, dealer incentives, and the importance of reading lease agreements carefully to avoid unexpected charges at vehicle return. Understanding what constitutes normal wear and tear versus damage that triggers costly fees can save hundreds of dollars when a lease concludes.

For consumers considering whether leasing makes financial sense for their situation, insights from automotive professionals provide valuable perspective on structuring a deal that aligns with their actual driving needs and budget constraints.

title: The Artist Who Created This Lace-Patterned Porsche 911S Bought It Back
summary: Dr. Yes painted this subversive art car in the 1980s. She's going to make sure it ends up in a museum.
whatHappening: An artist known as Dr. Yes has repurchased a Porsche 911S she customized with an intricate lace pattern in the 1980s, reclaiming the one-of-a-kind art car decades after its original sale. She now plans to ensure the vehicle finds a permanent home in a museum rather than remaining in private hands.
whoInvolved: Dr. Yes is a visual artist who created this subversive art car by hand-painting an elaborate lace pattern onto a Porsche 911S during the 1980s. The Porsche 911 is a high-performance sports car produced by Porsche of Stuttgart, Germany, first introduced in 1964 and known for its iconic rear-engine design.
whyMatters: The buyback represents a rare instance of an artist reclaiming and redirecting the legacy of her own work, asserting creative intent over market forces and private ownership. By securing the vehicle's placement in a museum, Dr. Yes ensures her 1980s conceptual intervention on automotive design will be preserved and contextualized for public view, rather than fade into obscurity or be altered by subsequent owners.
articleBody:
Dr. Yes, an artist known for her conceptual and subversive approach to visual creation, has successfully repurchased a Porsche 911S that she hand-painted with an elaborate lace pattern in the 1980s. The acquisition marks a significant moment for the artist, who now intends to donate or place the vehicle in a museum collection where it will be preserved as a permanent artwork and cultural artifact.

The lace-patterned 911S represents a bold artistic statement from its creation period. Rather than celebrate the car's performance specifications or sleek industrial design, Dr. Yes transformed the vehicle into a textile-inspired object, layering delicate, intricate patterns across its body. This approach challenged conventional notions of what constitutes art and how high-value consumer goods can be reimagined as creative canvases. The Porsche 911, first introduced by Porsche of Stuttgart, Germany in September 1964, has maintained its iconic status as a rear-engine sports car throughout its generations, making it a potent symbol of automotive prestige and performance.

According to Car and Driver, the artist's decision to buy back her own work underscores her commitment to controlling its final disposition and ensuring it reaches an institutional setting rather than remaining in the hands of private collectors who may not appreciate or preserve its conceptual significance. Such buybacks are uncommon in the art world, particularly when the original work has changed hands multiple times over several decades.

Museum placement would give the lace-patterned 911S the institutional legitimacy and conservation care it requires to endure as an artwork. Unlike functional vehicles that deteriorate through use, museum-held pieces benefit from climate control, professional restoration, and curatorial interpretation that situates them within art historical narratives. For Dr. Yes, this outcome represents a vindication of her 1980s vision—a time when painting elaborate patterns onto a luxury sports car was an unconventional gesture that may have seemed merely decorative to its original owner.

The story also reflects broader questions within contemporary art about ownership, authorship, and the boundary between craft and artistic statement. By reclaiming her creation, Dr. Yes asserts that the work's meaning and legacy belong neither to the market nor to intervening owners, but to the artist's original intention and vision.

title: 20 Years Ago, a Ride in a Tesla Roadster Changed Me
summary: It was my first-ever ride in an electric car, and it's led to many more.
whatHappening: A Car and Driver writer reflects on a transformative experience from two decades ago: a ride in a Tesla Roadster that introduced them to electric vehicles and set them on a path of continued EV exploration.
whoInvolved: Tesla, Inc., the American automotive and clean energy company headquartered in Austin, Texas, which designed and manufactured the original Tesla Roadster electric sports car between 2008 and 2012.
whyMatters: Personal testimonies about early EV experiences reveal how pioneering electric vehicles shaped attitudes toward clean transportation adoption. The story illustrates the long-term influence that a single memorable encounter with electric technology can have on an individual's relationship with mobility and sustainability.
articleBody:
Two decades can seem like a lifetime in the automotive world, yet some moments linger with particular clarity. For one writer, a single ride in a Tesla Roadster two decades ago proved to be a pivotal turning point—a moment that opened an entirely new chapter in their relationship with cars and driving. According to Car and Driver, that first-ever ride in an electric car has since led to many more experiences behind the wheel of EVs.

The Tesla Roadster that changed this driver's perspective was part of the first generation of the vehicle, produced by Tesla Motors between 2008 and 2012. During that era, electric cars were largely theoretical concepts in the minds of most consumers, relegated to environmental advocacy and science-fiction speculation. The Roadster, however, proved that an electric vehicle could be thrilling, performant, and desirable—a far cry from the slow, utilitarian golf carts many imagined when they thought of battery-powered transportation.

What made that initial ride so transformative wasn't simply the novelty of electric propulsion. Rather, it was the tangible realization that EV technology had matured enough to deliver a genuine driving experience. The acceleration, the responsiveness, the silence—these elements combined to challenge preconceived notions about what an electric car could be. For someone accustomed to conventional internal combustion engines, the experience was revelatory.

In the two decades since that pivotal ride, the landscape has shifted dramatically. Tesla, Inc., now a multinational automotive and clean energy company, has expanded far beyond the Roadster into a diverse lineup of battery electric vehicles, stationary battery storage systems, solar panels, and related products. The broader automotive industry has followed suit, with nearly every major manufacturer now committed to electrification strategies. What once seemed impossibly futuristic has become increasingly mainstream.

Yet the through-line remains personal. That single ride in a Roadster two decades ago proved sufficient to spark a curiosity that has only deepened with time. Each subsequent EV experience has reinforced the lessons of that first encounter: that electric vehicles represent not a compromise but a genuine alternative worthy of enthusiasm and continued exploration. For this driver, and countless others similarly awakened to the possibilities of clean transportation, the Roadster served as more than a car—it was a gateway.

title: 2000 Corbin Sparrow Lands On Bring a Trailer
summary: Back in 2000, EVs were pretty weird.
whatHappening: A 2000 Corbin Sparrow, an early electric vehicle from the era when EVs were still novelties, has appeared for sale on Bring a Trailer, the online marketplace for enthusiast vehicles. The listing offers collectors a rare glimpse into automotive history from two decades ago.
whoInvolved: Corbin Motors, the manufacturer behind the Sparrow, was an early pioneer in personal electric vehicles during the late 1990s and early 2000s. The company later transitioned to Myers Motors, which continued producing three-wheeled electric commuter vehicles into the 2010s.
whyMatters: The sale highlights how far electric vehicle technology and consumer acceptance have evolved since 2000, when EVs were considered quirky alternatives rather than mainstream options. This particular vehicle serves as a tangible artifact of the EV movement's early, experimental phase, before Tesla and other manufacturers brought the category into the mainstream consciousness.
articleBody:
A 2000 Corbin Sparrow has surfaced on Bring a Trailer, one of the internet's premier marketplaces for unusual and collectible vehicles. According to Car and Driver, back in 2000, EVs were pretty weird—and this particular machine is a perfect embodiment of that era's boldly unconventional approach to electric propulsion.

The Sparrow represents a specific moment in automotive history when manufacturers were exploring radically different form factors for battery-powered vehicles. Corbin Motors designed the Sparrow as a practical urban commuter, though its unconventional three-wheeled design and minimal footprint made it a curiosity rather than a mainstream choice. The vehicle emerged from the same lineage that would later produce the Myers Motors NmG, a single-passenger, three-wheeled battery electric vehicle that the company manufactured from 1999 into the early 2010s specifically for commuting and city driving. After 2005, production shifted to Myers Motors, which continued refining the concept as a personal electric vehicle (PEV) category was still being defined.

What makes the Sparrow's appearance on Bring a Trailer significant is the broader context it provides for understanding EV development. In 2000, the technology was vastly more limited than today—batteries offered shorter ranges, charging infrastructure was virtually nonexistent, and the vehicles themselves carried the stigma of being science-fair experiments rather than serious transportation. Yet manufacturers like Corbin pushed forward with earnest attempts to solve real urban mobility problems, even if their solutions looked bizarre by modern standards.

The sale of this particular 2000 model offers collectors and enthusiasts a tangible piece of that experimental era. Bring a Trailer's platform has become known for surfacing forgotten automotive oddities and giving them a second life with preservationists who recognize their historical value. A Corbin Sparrow from the turn of the millennium falls squarely into that category—it's a vehicle that was ahead of its time conceptually, even if the execution and technology felt alien to most drivers in 2000.

Today's EV market has rendered the Sparrow a historical curio. Modern electric vehicles offer dramatically longer ranges, faster charging, and performance that would have seemed miraculous to Corbin engineers. Yet the Sparrow's existence underscores an important truth: the push toward electrified transportation didn't begin with Elon Musk or recent policy incentives. Visionary manufacturers were already building electric vehicles two decades ago, experimenting with geometry and functionality in ways that feel both earnest and endearingly awkward in retrospect.

title: Ram Rumble Bee-Based Hennessey Maximus Is a 1000-HP Street Truck
summary: Hennessey teased the hi-po pickup that features a supercharged Hellcat V-8, a prominent rear wing, and a claimed 200-mph top speed.
whatHappening: Hennessey Performance Engineering has teased a heavily modified Ram pickup truck called the Rumble Bee-Based Maximus, equipped with a supercharged Hellcat V-8 engine producing 1000 horsepower. The high-performance truck features an aggressive rear wing and claims a top speed of 200 mph.
whoInvolved: Hennessey Performance Engineering is an American automotive tuning company and sports car manufacturer known for building extreme performance vehicles. Ram is a full-size pickup truck brand manufactured by Stellantis North America and marketed since 2010.
whyMatters: This project signals the continued trend of ultra-high-performance street trucks blending luxury with raw power, appealing to enthusiasts willing to pay premium prices for one-off builds. The 1000-hp specification and 200-mph capability push the boundaries of what pickup trucks can achieve in acceleration and top speed, potentially influencing consumer expectations and competitor offerings in the performance truck segment.
articleBody:
Hennessey Performance Engineering has unveiled plans for an extreme pickup truck modification that combines the practicality of a Ram truck with supercar-level performance. The Rumble Bee-Based Hennessey Maximus, according to Car and Driver, features a supercharged Hellcat V-8 engine and a striking rear wing, with the tuner claiming the vehicle can reach 200 miles per hour.

The engine package represents the centerpiece of the build. By leveraging the supercharged Hellcat V-8—a proven powerplant known for delivering exceptional output—Hennessey aims to extract 1000 horsepower from the modified truck. This power figure places the Maximus in rarified territory, as most production trucks max out well below such numbers. The engineering challenge of integrating a supercharged engine of this caliber into a pickup platform designed for hauling and towing demands significant chassis and drivetrain modifications.

The aesthetic modifications signal that this is no ordinary work truck. The prominent rear wing, a component typically found on race cars and high-performance supercars, gives the Maximus a visually aggressive stance. This styling choice underscores Hennessey's philosophy: creating a street truck that performs as dramatically as it looks. Such visual cues serve both functional and psychological purposes, telegraphing the vehicle's performance capability to observers.

Hennessey Performance Engineering has built a reputation as an automotive tuning company willing to tackle ambitious performance projects. Ram, manufactured by Stellantis North America and marketed since 2010, has become a popular donor platform for high-performance builds as the current generation offers modern chassis technology and structural integrity capable of handling significant power increases. The pairing of Hennessey's tuning expertise with Ram's platform appears designed to create a showcase vehicle that demonstrates what is possible when conventional truck architecture meets unlimited performance ambition.

The claimed 200-mph top speed would make the Maximus one of the fastest production or modified trucks ever built. Achieving such speeds requires not only raw horsepower but also aerodynamic refinement, braking capability, and suspension tuning—elements that suggest Hennessey's build goes far beyond a simple engine upgrade. While details remain limited at the teasing stage, the specifications hint at a comprehensive overhaul aimed at creating a functional yet extreme street vehicle.

title: VW Is Reportedly Developing a New Pickup Truck for the United States
summary: Despite talks of cutting its global product lineup in half, Volkswagen is allegedly working on a new pickup truck for the United States.
whatHappening: Volkswagen is reportedly developing a new pickup truck for the United States market, despite the company's stated plans to cut its global product lineup in half. The move signals the automaker's commitment to the American truck segment even as it pursues broader cost-reduction strategies.
whoInvolved: Volkswagen is a German automobile manufacturer based in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony, established in 1937 and now a major global automotive conglomerate with a market capitalization of approximately US$58.9 billion as of 2025. The company has previous experience in the pickup truck market through its Volkswagen Amarok, a mid-size pickup produced since 2010.
whyMatters: The development of a new U.S. pickup signals VW's strategic focus on high-demand American markets despite portfolio consolidation efforts elsewhere. Success in the competitive American truck segment could strengthen VW's position and revenue in one of the world's largest automotive markets, though it also underscores potential tensions between the company's stated efficiency goals and product expansion plans.
articleBody:
Volkswagen is moving forward with development of a new pickup truck for the United States, according to Car and Driver, even as the German automaker has publicly discussed cutting its global product lineup in half. The reported project represents a notable commitment to the American market, where full-size and mid-size pickup trucks remain among the best-selling vehicle categories.

Volkswagen already has experience in the pickup truck segment through its Volkswagen Amarok, a mid-size pickup that has been in production since 2010. The Amarok features a body-on-frame construction with double-wishbone suspension at the front and leaf springs at the rear, and is offered in both single-cab and double-cab configurations with rear-wheel drive or four-wheel-drive options. The vehicle is powered by turbocharged petrol or turbocharged direct-injection diesel engines, providing the kind of powertrain flexibility that appeals to truck buyers in various markets.

The timing of this reported U.S. pickup development is noteworthy given Volkswagen's broader strategic discussions. The company, which is based in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony, and has grown into a global automotive powerhouse since its establishment in 1937, has indicated plans to streamline its offerings to improve efficiency and reduce costs. A market capitalization of approximately US$58.9 billion as of 2025 reflects the scale of the organization, but also the competitive pressures driving such consolidation efforts.

The American pickup truck market remains one of the world's most lucrative and competitive segments, dominated by established players. For Volkswagen, a new U.S. truck could represent both an opportunity to capture market share and a test of the brand's ability to compete in a category where brand loyalty and reputation for durability are paramount. The company's decision to pursue this project despite broader portfolio reduction plans suggests confidence in the segment's profitability and growth potential.

Until now, Volkswagen has not offered a modern pickup truck specifically designed for the American market, limiting its ability to compete in this high-volume segment. A purpose-built U.S. truck could allow the brand to expand its footprint among truck-focused buyers and potentially create synergies with its existing dealer network and customer base.

title: These Drift-Spec Dodge Chargers Have 750 HP and a Manual
summary: Dodge revealed a pair of one-off Chargers that turned the standard Scat Pack models into drifting machines.
whatHappening: Dodge has unveiled two custom-built Chargers stripped down and rebuilt as dedicated drift cars, each packing 750 horsepower and equipped with a manual transmission. These one-off vehicles transform the standard Scat Pack performance lineup into machines purpose-built for controlled slides and extreme cornering.
whoInvolved: Dodge, the American automotive brand and division of Stellantis based in Auburn Hills, Michigan, created these vehicles. Dodge has a long history of producing performance cars and has been marketing the Charger model across eight generations since 1966.
whyMatters: The drift-spec Chargers demonstrate Dodge's continued commitment to performance customization and manual transmission options at a time when automatics dominate the market. The move signals the brand's engagement with drift culture and enthusiasts seeking hardcore, track-focused versions of production vehicles.
articleBody:
Dodge has taken two of its Scat Pack Chargers and transformed them into purpose-built drift machines, each delivering 750 horsepower and equipped with a manual transmission. According to Car and Driver, these are one-off builds, meaning they represent custom, unique creations rather than a production line expansion.

The Charger has been a cornerstone of Dodge's performance portfolio since its introduction in 1966, and the brand has long positioned itself as an American manufacturer of high-output vehicles. The Scat Pack lineup represents the modern iteration of that performance heritage, and converting these models into dedicated drift platforms extends that legacy into specialized motorsport territory.

Drift racing demands specific mechanical modifications beyond what factory performance models offer. A manual transmission is essential for the heel-and-toe downshifting and throttle control that drift technique requires, making the inclusion of a stick shift particularly notable on a modern muscle car. The 750-horsepower figure indicates substantial engine tuning and optimization, likely including upgrades to forced induction, fuel delivery, and internal engine components.

These one-off builds suggest Dodge's interest in demonstrating what its performance platform can achieve when pushed to extremes. Rather than releasing a production drift variant, the company has created showcase vehicles that can be used for promotional purposes, motorsport events, or customer experiences. This approach allows Dodge to explore niche performance segments without the investment required for a full production run.

The drift-spec Chargers also reflect broader enthusiasm within the automotive community for manual transmissions and analog driving experiences. As many manufacturers phase out stick shifts in favor of automatics, builds like these appeal to purists and enthusiasts who value driver engagement and the tactile feedback of a clutch pedal.

title: 2027 Dodge Charger Super Bee Brings 600 HP and Track-Focused Hardware
summary: The new Super Bee is the most powerful six-cylinder Charger, and it debuts a host of new features designed for faster lap times.
whatHappening: Dodge has unveiled the 2027 Charger Super Bee, a track-focused muscle car powered by a 600-horsepower six-cylinder engine. The new model marks a revival of the Super Bee nameplate and introduces performance-oriented hardware designed to deliver faster lap times.
whoInvolved: Dodge, the American automaker owned by Stellantis, is behind the 2027 Super Bee revival. The company has been marketing the Charger since 1966 across eight generations, and is now resurrecting the Super Bee badge, which was last produced as a muscle car in 1971.
whyMatters: The 2027 Super Bee signals Dodge's commitment to performance vehicles in an era of electrification, offering enthusiasts a six-cylinder alternative with significant horsepower. The track-focused engineering represents an effort to compete in the high-performance segment while maintaining the muscle-car heritage that defined the original Super Bee era.
articleBody:
Dodge has reignited one of muscle-car history's most iconic nameplates with the introduction of the 2027 Charger Super Bee, a track-ready vehicle that delivers 600 horsepower from a six-cylinder powertrain. According to Car and Driver, this new iteration represents the most powerful six-cylinder Charger ever built, combining classic branding with contemporary performance engineering.

The Super Bee badge carries significant weight in automotive history. Originally marketed by Dodge as a mid-sized muscle car from 1968 through 1971, the Super Bee became synonymous with American performance and aggressive styling. The nameplate also enjoyed a extended run in Mexico, where it was based on a compact Chrysler platform and remained in production from 1970 until 1980. By reviving the Super Bee name for the modern Charger lineup, Dodge is tapping into decades of brand recognition and nostalgia among enthusiasts.

The 2027 model introduces a suite of track-focused hardware engineered to maximize performance on the circuit. While specific technical details remain limited, the emphasis on lap-time improvements suggests the Super Bee incorporates enhanced suspension geometry, braking systems, and aerodynamic refinements beyond the standard Charger platform. This approach positions the Super Bee as a driver-oriented vehicle rather than a purely casual cruiser.

The six-cylinder engine choice reflects Dodge's strategic direction in an automotive landscape increasingly concerned with efficiency and emissions. Rather than relying on traditional large-displacement V8 powerplants, the 600-horsepower six-cylinder demonstrates that manufacturers can achieve substantial performance through advanced engineering. This represents a pragmatic balance between maintaining the muscle-car identity that customers expect and meeting modern regulatory requirements.

The Charger itself has maintained a prominent place in Dodge's lineup since its 1966 debut, spanning eight generations of evolution. The new Super Bee variant adds a performance-oriented tier to that legacy, appealing to buyers who prioritize track capability and distinctive branding. As the automotive industry continues its transition toward electrification, offerings like the Super Bee may represent a final chapter for traditional high-performance internal-combustion vehicles from major manufacturers.

title: Driver of the Week: —Ed
summary: Meet —Ed, C/D's Backfires editor, commentator, kibbitzer, life coach, and resident crank.
whatHappening: Car and Driver has named —Ed as its Driver of the Week, recognizing the staff member who serves as the publication's Backfires editor and regular commentator. The honor celebrates —Ed's multifaceted role spanning editorial work, opinion pieces, coaching, and cantankerous takes on automotive culture.
whoInvolved: —Ed is a longstanding member of Car and Driver's editorial team, one of the automotive industry's most established and influential publications. Car and Driver has built its reputation over decades as a leading voice in car journalism, known for combining technical expertise with opinionated commentary on driving culture and industry trends.
whyMatters: The recognition underscores the value Car and Driver places on personalities and distinctive voices in automotive journalism, where individual perspective and point of view drive reader engagement. —Ed's appointment highlights the publication's investment in commentary-driven content alongside traditional news and reviews, a format increasingly central to how automotive media reaches and retains audiences.
articleBody:
Car and Driver has selected —Ed as its Driver of the Week, a regular feature celebrating members of the publication's staff and their contributions to automotive journalism. The honor recognizes —Ed's wide-ranging role across the outlet's editorial operations, where the writer serves as editor of Backfires—the publication's opinion and commentary section—while also appearing regularly as a commentator and kibbitzer on automotive matters.

According to Car and Driver, —Ed brings a distinctive voice to the publication's coverage, one characterized by candor and an unvarnished perspective on industry developments, driving culture, and the automotive landscape. The appointment as "resident crank" signals the publication's embrace of opinionated voices, a strategy that reflects broader shifts in automotive media toward personality-driven content alongside traditional car reviews and news reporting.

—Ed's role as Backfires editor places the writer at the center of Car and Driver's commentary operation, a section devoted to essays, takes, and arguments about cars and driving. The position requires editorial judgment in curating and shaping pieces that often challenge prevailing industry wisdom or cultural assumptions about automobiles and their place in American life. Beyond editorial duties, —Ed's visibility as a commentator and life coach suggests a broader engagement with Car and Driver's audience, extending influence beyond the written page.

The Driver of the Week recognition reflects the automotive publication's investment in cultivating distinctive personalities within its masthead. In an era where automotive journalism competes with social media, YouTube channels, and manufacturer-controlled content for reader attention, editorial voices that express clear perspective and personality have become increasingly valuable. —Ed's appointment underscores this shift, positioning individual viewpoint and editorial stance as worthy of celebration alongside traditional journalistic accomplishments.

For Car and Driver, the regular Driver of the Week feature serves as both a morale tool for staff and a signal to readers about which voices matter most to the publication's editorial vision. By honoring —Ed's work across editing, commentary, and opinion-making, the publication reinforces its commitment to a particular approach to automotive journalism: one that prizes skepticism, personality, and the willingness to take stands on industry and culture.

title: The Next-Gen 2029 Chevy Camaro Will Reportedly Have Four Doors
summary: The new Camaro has been delayed until the 2029 model year and will have two more doors than before, according to a report.
whatHappening: Chevrolet has delayed the redesigned Camaro until the 2029 model year and will introduce a significant design change: the iconic two-door pony car will become a four-door sedan. This represents a major shift in the vehicle's identity after more than five decades as a two-door competitor.
whoInvolved: Chevrolet, General Motors' mainstream automotive brand, is behind the redesign. The Camaro has been a flagship pony car since its 1967 debut, designed to compete directly with the Ford Mustang and built on platforms shared with other GM vehicles like the Pontiac Firebird.
whyMatters: The shift to four doors signals how traditional American performance cars are evolving to meet changing consumer preferences and market demands. The delay until 2029 also suggests extended development timelines as automakers balance electrification, design, and profitability concerns in a competitive segment.
articleBody:
Chevrolet is making a dramatic shift with its next-generation Camaro, trading the iconic two-door configuration for a four-door layout when the vehicle returns in 2029, according to Car and Driver. The redesigned Camaro will mark a significant departure from the pony car's traditional formula that has defined the nameplate since its introduction.

The Chevrolet Camaro first went on sale on September 29, 1966, for the 1967 model year, and was created specifically to compete with the Ford Mustang in the growing pony car segment. Throughout its history, the Camaro has remained true to its two-door design, establishing itself as a performance-oriented vehicle. The shift to four doors suggests Chevrolet is repositioning the model to appeal to a broader audience seeking practicality alongside performance.

The delayed timeline is notable in itself. The postponement until the 2029 model year gives Chevrolet additional development time as the automotive industry undergoes rapid transformation. The decision to add two doors indicates the company is willing to fundamentally reimagine the vehicle rather than deliver an incremental update. This approach suggests extensive engineering and design work is underway to ensure the new Camaro meets modern safety standards, emissions requirements, and consumer expectations.

Historically, the Camaro shared its platform and major components with other General Motors vehicles, including the Pontiac Firebird, which was also introduced for the 1967 model year. This shared-platform approach allowed GM to maximize efficiency while delivering distinct vehicles to different market segments. The next-generation Camaro will likely follow a similar strategy, leveraging GM's existing architectures to support the four-door configuration.

The move to four doors aligns with broader industry trends toward larger, more versatile vehicles, even within performance segments. Consumers increasingly prioritize rear-seat space and cargo capacity, and a four-door design naturally accommodates these preferences. For Chevrolet, the redesign offers an opportunity to modernize the Camaro while maintaining its core identity as a performance vehicle.

With the redesign still years away, full specifications and powertrain details remain unknown. However, the fundamental design change already signals that Chevrolet is committing significant resources to reimagining one of its most storied nameplates for the next generation of buyers.

title: 2027 Toyota Prius PHEV
summary: Review, Pricing, and Specs
whatHappening: Toyota is introducing a 2027 model year Prius plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV), combining the automaker's long-running hybrid nameplate with plug-in charging capability. Car and Driver is providing an early review, pricing details, and full specifications on the upcoming model.
whoInvolved: Toyota, the Japanese automaker behind the Prius since its 1997 debut, is launching this new plug-in variant. Car and Driver, a major automotive journalism outlet, is covering the vehicle's arrival with comprehensive review and spec information.
whyMatters: The 2027 Prius PHEV represents Toyota's effort to offer consumers greater electric-driving range alongside traditional hybrid efficiency, as automakers balance transition to electrification with plug-in flexibility. For buyers seeking reduced fuel consumption and emissions with the convenience of home charging, this model bridges the gap between conventional hybrids and fully electric vehicles during a critical period of powertrain evolution.
articleBody:
Toyota is refreshing its iconic Prius lineup for 2027 with a plug-in hybrid variant designed to give drivers extended all-electric driving capability while retaining the fuel efficiency that made the original model famous. According to Car and Driver, the new PHEV version brings together Toyota's proven Hybrid Synergy Drive system with rechargeable battery technology that allows owners to charge via an external power source—a departure from conventional hybrids that rely solely on internal combustion engines and regenerative braking to power their electric motors.

The Prius has evolved significantly since its 1997 introduction as a subcompact four-door sedan. For more than two decades, the nameplate has served as Toyota's flagship for demonstrating that hybrid technology could be both practical and popular with mainstream buyers. Since 2003, all Prius models have been built as compact five-door liftbacks, a body style that balances passenger space with aerodynamic efficiency. The addition of plug-in capability to this established platform extends Toyota's hybrid leadership into the PHEV segment, where buyers want greater electric-only range without committing fully to battery-electric powertrains.

Plug-in hybrids occupy a distinctive market position. Unlike traditional hybrids that charge only from engine power and braking, PHEVs like this new Prius variant allow owners to replenish their battery packs by plugging into household or public charging stations. This dual-power approach appeals to drivers with predictable daily commutes who could run on battery power most days while retaining gasoline backup for longer journeys. The 2027 Prius PHEV combines that flexibility with Toyota's reputation for reliability and fuel economy.

The automaker is releasing the new model at a pivotal moment in the automotive industry. Regulatory pressure and consumer interest in electrification continue to accelerate, yet many buyers remain hesitant about fully electric vehicles due to charging infrastructure concerns and upfront costs. Plug-in hybrids bridge this gap by offering reduced tailpipe emissions and lower fuel costs for typical driving patterns while eliminating range anxiety for weekend trips or cross-country travel.

Car and Driver's coverage includes detailed pricing and complete specifications, helping prospective buyers understand what the 2027 model delivers. The review should clarify key questions about battery capacity, all-electric range, total output when both drivetrain systems work together, and how the plug-in variant's efficiency and real-world performance compare to the conventional hybrid Prius. Such details matter significantly for consumers deciding between hybrid and plug-in hybrid options.

title: 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT53: A 536-HP EV That Makes Straight-Six Sounds
summary: It's less powerful than the 1153-hp GT63, but this new entry-level variant will still be plenty quick.
whatHappening: Mercedes-AMG is introducing a new entry-level GT53 variant for 2027 that runs on electric power and produces 536 horsepower. Despite being significantly less powerful than the 1153-hp GT63 model, the EV will deliver impressive performance while featuring a unique straight-six sound profile.
whoInvolved: Mercedes-AMG, the high-performance subsidiary of Mercedes-Benz AG headquartered in Affalterbach, Germany, is developing this new variant. Mercedes-Benz AG, the Stuttgart-based German luxury automaker founded in 1926, manufactures the GT lineup under its AMG performance brand.
whyMatters: The GT53 EV represents Mercedes-AMG's continued shift toward electrification while maintaining performance credentials and brand identity. This entry-level option could expand the high-performance EV market by offering accessible performance to a broader customer base, signaling how traditional luxury performance brands are adapting their powertrains for the electric era.
articleBody:
Mercedes-AMG is preparing to launch a new entry-level variant of its iconic GT sports car, the 2027 GT53, which will mark a significant milestone for the performance brand: a fully electric iteration that delivers 536 horsepower while emulating the auditory signature of a straight-six engine. According to Car and Driver, this new model will be less powerful than the conventional 1153-hp GT63, yet will still offer the acceleration and handling characteristics expected from Mercedes-AMG's elite performance lineup.

The introduction of the GT53 EV underscores Mercedes-AMG's broader electrification strategy. As the high-performance subsidiary of Mercedes-Benz AG—the Stuttgart-based German automaker founded in 1926—AMG has historically focused on optimizing conventional powertrains through engineering innovation and customization. The shift to electric propulsion represents a fundamental pivot in how the brand approaches performance, moving from internal combustion horsepower races to electric motor efficiency and instant torque delivery.

One of the most intriguing aspects of the GT53 is its engineered sound design. Electric vehicles traditionally lack the mechanical noise signatures that enthusiasts associate with performance cars, particularly the distinctive rumble of a multi-cylinder engine. By programming a straight-six sound profile into the EV, Mercedes-AMG is attempting to preserve a crucial element of the driving experience and brand heritage, even as the underlying technology becomes fully electric.

The 536-hp output positions the GT53 as an accessible entry point into the GT family for performance-minded buyers. While substantially outgunned on paper by the GT63, the electric variant's instant torque characteristics and the responsiveness typical of EV powertrains could allow it to feel more agile in real-world driving. This performance democratization aligns with broader trends in the luxury automotive sector, where electrification is expanding rather than contracting the performance segment.

For Mercedes-Benz AG and its AMG division, the GT53 EV also represents a strategic response to competitive pressures in the electric performance market. Other luxury brands have begun populating the high-performance EV space, and offering multiple variants of an iconic nameplate helps AMG maintain its positioning as a premier performance authority while transitioning its portfolio toward electrification.

The 2027 model year timing suggests that development and regulatory certification are well underway, indicating a serious commitment to bringing this vehicle to market within the decade. As the automotive industry continues its acceleration toward electrification, models like the GT53 will increasingly define what performance means for the next generation of luxury car buyers.

title: Heated Seats Are Way More Popular Than AWD Among New-Car Shoppers
summary: A new survey found that heated seats ranked higher on drivers' new-car wishlists than parking sensors, adaptive cruise control, and all-wheel drive.
whatHappening: A new survey reveals that heated seats have become a more sought-after feature among new-car buyers than several traditionally popular technologies. Drivers are ranking heated seats above parking sensors, adaptive cruise control, and all-wheel drive on their wishlists.
whoInvolved: Car and Driver, the automotive publication that conducted the survey, tracked consumer preferences across various vehicle features and technologies. The survey reflects the priorities of new-car shoppers making purchasing decisions in today's market.
whyMatters: The finding signals a shift in consumer priorities toward comfort and convenience features over performance and safety technology. This data matters to automakers planning feature packages and trim levels, as it reveals what features actually drive purchase decisions rather than what manufacturers assume buyers want.
articleBody:
New-car shoppers are prioritizing comfort over cutting-edge technology in ways that might surprise some in the automotive industry. According to Car and Driver, a new survey found that heated seats ranked higher on drivers' wishlists than several features manufacturers have long emphasized as key selling points. The finding challenges conventional wisdom about what buyers actually value when making one of the largest purchases of their lives.

Heated seats emerged as a more popular feature than parking sensors, which assist drivers in tight spaces and have become increasingly common on new vehicles. The preference also extended to adaptive cruise control, a semi-autonomous driving technology that automatically adjusts speed based on traffic conditions. Most strikingly, heated seats outranked all-wheel drive—a powertrain option that has been heavily marketed as essential for safety and capability, particularly in regions with winter weather.

The survey results point to a fundamental mismatch between what automakers prioritize and what buyers actually want. While manufacturers have invested heavily in advanced driver-assistance systems and performance upgrades, consumers appear more motivated by features that directly improve their daily comfort. Heated seats represent an accessible luxury that delivers immediate, tangible benefits during cold months, making the appeal straightforward and universal.

This preference may reflect broader economic and lifestyle considerations among car shoppers. Heated seats offer practical comfort at a relatively modest cost compared to major powertrain or technology packages, making them attractive across multiple price points and market segments. The feature works equally well for a luxury sedan buyer and an economy-car shopper, eliminating the prestige positioning that might surround more specialized technologies.

The data carries implications for how automakers structure their trim levels and optional equipment packages. If heated seats consistently rank as a high-demand feature, manufacturers may need to make them standard or readily accessible rather than burying them in upper-tier packages. The survey suggests that understanding actual consumer behavior—rather than relying on assumptions about tech-forward preferences—should drive decisions about which features to emphasize and where to invest in product development.

title: Vote for This Awesome Colin McRae Subaru Rally Lego Set
summary: If enough fans back this design, it could have a chance at becoming a real Lego set.
whatHappening: A Lego set design featuring Colin McRae's iconic Subaru rally car is now open for fan voting. If the design receives enough support, it could be produced as an official Lego set.
whoInvolved: Lego, the Danish toy company behind the fan-design platform; Colin McRae, the legendary British rally driver who won the 1995 World Rally Championship; and Subaru, whose World Rally Team fielded McRae's distinctive blue-and-yellow cars throughout the 1990s.
whyMatters: This represents a rare intersection of automotive heritage and consumer product design, allowing fans to directly influence which pieces of racing history get immortalized in toy form. A successful campaign could introduce McRae's legacy and Subaru's rally dominance to a new generation of enthusiasts and collectors.
articleBody:
A newly designed Lego set commemorating Colin McRae's legendary Subaru rally car is now available for fan votes on the Lego Ideas platform, according to Car and Driver. If the design garners sufficient community support, it could join Lego's official product lineup as a finished set.

Colin McRae remains one of rally racing's most celebrated figures. The British driver claimed the 1991 and 1992 British Rally Championships before making history in 1995 as the first British driver to win the World Rally Championship Drivers' title. His success came largely during his years with Subaru's World Rally Team, where he piloted the manufacturer's now-iconic blue-and-yellow machines that became synonymous with the sport.

The distinctive color scheme McRae's cars carried—Subaru's signature blue paired with bright yellow—originated from the team's sponsorship deal with State Express 555, a BAT cigarette brand that was particularly popular in Asia. This livery appeared on Subaru vehicles from 1993 to 2003, with particular prominence in the mid-1990s when McRae was at his peak. The combination has since become instantly recognizable to rally fans and remains culturally significant in automotive circles, even decades after tobacco sponsorship was phased out.

The Lego Ideas platform allows designers to submit original creations and pitch them to the broader Lego community. Sets that accumulate sufficient votes are then reviewed for potential production and commercial release. The McRae Subaru design taps into nostalgia for a golden era of rally racing while appealing to both automotive enthusiasts and Lego collectors who value licensed or historically significant builds.

Subaru's World Rally Team itself dates back to 1980, though the program achieved its greatest prominence in the 1990s under British firm Prodrive's management. That decade saw the manufacturer establish itself as a dominant force in world rally competition, with drivers like McRae piloting the distinctive blue machines to numerous victories and championships. For fans of that era, a Lego recreation of McRae's car represents a tangible way to celebrate a transformative period in both the driver's career and Subaru's motorsport legacy.

title: 2027 Ferrari Amalfi Spider Driven: Turn On, Tune In, Drop Top
summary: Ferrari's newest entry-level GT convertible demands that you live in the moment.
whatHappening: Ferrari has unveiled the 2027 Amalfi Spider, its newest entry-level GT convertible, positioning it as a vehicle designed for drivers who prioritize living in the present moment. Car and Driver has driven the new model and filed their impressions.
whoInvolved: Ferrari S.p.A., the Italian luxury sports car manufacturer based in Maranello, is behind the Amalfi Spider. Founded by Enzo Ferrari in 1939 and spun off as an independent public company in 2016, Ferrari continues to expand its road car lineup with new models targeting different buyer segments.
whyMatters: The Amalfi Spider represents Ferrari's strategy to broaden its market reach with an accessible convertible GT offering, potentially attracting buyers seeking the brand's prestige in a more lifestyle-focused package. As an entry-level model, it signals how even luxury automakers are balancing performance credentials with approachability in an evolving market.
articleBody:
Ferrari's latest addition to its convertible lineup, the 2027 Amalfi Spider, arrives as the brand's newest entry-level grand tourer with a design philosophy centered on present-moment driving. According to Car and Driver, the vehicle prioritizes an engaging, immersive experience that encourages owners to focus on the act of driving rather than accumulating features or specifications.

The Amalfi Spider continues Ferrari's long tradition of accessible yet desirable vehicles. Since Ferrari began producing its current line of road cars in 1947, the manufacturer has refined the art of creating entry-level models that maintain the brand's performance and design DNA while broadening appeal. The convertible format has remained a cornerstone of Ferrari's portfolio, offering buyers the freedom of open-air driving combined with grand touring capability.

As an entry-level GT, the Amalfi Spider occupies a strategic position in Ferrari's model range. The car emphasizes the sensory elements of driving—engine response, handling feel, and the connection between driver and machine—rather than technological excess. This design direction reflects a broader philosophy that values mechanical engagement and real-time driver feedback, elements central to Ferrari's identity since Enzo Ferrari's founding vision in 1939.

The convertible format adds a distinctive dimension to the entry-level segment, allowing drivers to experience the Italian landscape and road conditions directly. This openness to the environment aligns with the car's philosophical approach: removing barriers between driver and experience, encouraging focus on driving dynamics rather than distraction.

For Ferrari, now operating as a fully independent company since its 2016 spinoff from Fiat Chrysler Automobiles, the Amalfi Spider represents a calculated effort to maintain accessibility within the luxury sports car category. The model aims to attract buyers seeking Ferrari's heritage and performance credentials without requiring the investment level of higher-tier offerings. The emphasis on present-moment engagement rather than technological ostentation distinguishes this entry into an increasingly crowded convertible GT market.

title: Ram Axes Hybrid Hemis and Stop-Start Tech in New 1500 Models
summary: Ram will phase out its hybrid V-8s and automatic stop-start technology in 2027 half-ton trucks, though some hybrids will still be available.
whatHappening: Ram is discontinuing hybrid V-8 engines and automatic stop-start technology in its new 1500 half-ton pickup trucks starting in 2027, though some hybrid options will remain available. The move marks a significant shift in the truck maker's powertrain strategy.
whoInvolved: Ram Trucks, the American pickup truck division of Stellantis North America, is making this decision. The brand, which spun off from Dodge in 2009 and manufactures its Ram 1500 pickups at Sterling Heights Assembly in Michigan, has built its reputation around performance and capability.
whyMatters: This decision signals a retreat from fuel-efficiency technologies that have become industry standard, potentially affecting Ram's competitive position as emissions regulations tighten and consumer preferences shift toward electrification. The move could impact buyer choice and may reflect challenges in consumer acceptance of hybrid drivetrains in the truck market.
articleBody:
Ram will phase out hybrid V-8 engines and automatic stop-start technology from its new 1500 half-ton trucks beginning in 2027, according to Car and Driver. The decision represents a notable reversal in the truck manufacturer's electrification strategy, even as some hybrid powertrains will continue to be offered in the lineup.

Ram Trucks, a division of Stellantis North America that was established in 2009 as a spin-off from Dodge, has traditionally emphasized performance and capability under its "Guts. Glory. Ram" slogan. The company manufactures its Ram 1500 pickups at Sterling Heights Assembly in Sterling Heights, Michigan. The 1500, as a half-ton truck, represents the brand's most popular and commercially significant vehicle segment.

The discontinuation of hybrid V-8s and stop-start systems in 2027 comes as the automotive industry grapples with balancing fuel efficiency, emissions compliance, and consumer preferences. Stop-start technology, which shuts down the engine at idle to reduce fuel consumption, has become increasingly common across vehicle categories. Hybrid V-8s, meanwhile, offer a middle ground between traditional gasoline engines and fully electric powertrains, providing improved efficiency without sacrificing towing capacity or performance.

Ram's decision to retain some hybrid options while eliminating others suggests the company is recalibrating its approach to powertrain offerings based on market demand and production priorities. The partial retention of hybrid technology indicates the brand is not abandoning electrification entirely, but rather focusing resources elsewhere.

The timing of the 2027 phase-out aligns with broader industry transitions, as manufacturers adjust their lineups in response to evolving federal emissions standards and shifting consumer purchasing patterns. For Ram customers, the move could mean fewer choices for fuel-efficient powertrains in the 1500 lineup during the next generation of trucks.

title: Ram's Rumble Bee Supercharger Kit Gives the Street Truck up to 900 HP
summary: Through the factory-backed Direct Connection, customers can also add a cat-back exhaust, distinct decals, and a lowered suspension.
whatHappening: Ram Trucks has launched a Rumble Bee Supercharger Kit through its factory-backed Direct Connection division, offering Street Truck customers up to 900 horsepower. The package includes performance upgrades alongside aesthetic and suspension modifications for a complete enhancement package.
whoInvolved: Ram Trucks, a division of Stellantis North America established in 2009 as a spin-off from Dodge, is behind the offering through its Direct Connection factory-backed customization program. The initiative targets customers seeking high-performance upgrades for their Ram Street Trucks.
whyMatters: The supercharger kit represents Ram's strategy to compete in the high-performance truck segment by offering factory-authorized power increases that appeal to enthusiasts. This direct-to-consumer approach through Direct Connection allows Ram to capture the customization market while maintaining brand control over quality and warranty implications.
articleBody:
Ram Trucks is amplifying the performance credentials of its Street Truck lineup with the introduction of a Rumble Bee Supercharger Kit capable of delivering up to 900 horsepower. The power upgrade arrives through Ram's Direct Connection program, the company's factory-backed customization division that enables customers to tailor their vehicles with manufacturer-approved enhancements.

Beyond the supercharger itself, the kit offers a comprehensive suite of modifications designed to maximize both performance and visual impact. According to Car and Driver, customers can add a cat-back exhaust system to complement the power gains, along with distinct decals that signal the truck's enhanced capabilities and a lowered suspension that improves handling dynamics. This bundled approach transforms the Street Truck into a more aggressive and capable machine without requiring owners to source components from multiple aftermarket suppliers.

Ram Trucks, a division of Stellantis North America, has positioned itself as a full-spectrum truck brand since its establishment in 2009 as a spin-off of Dodge, maintaining the iconic ram logo that was originally associated with its parent brand. The company's marketing heritage centers on the "Guts. Glory. Ram." slogan, a messaging framework that naturally extends to performance-focused offerings like the Rumble Bee Supercharger Kit. By channeling upgrades through Direct Connection rather than leaving performance customization entirely to independent shops, Ram maintains quality control and brand coherence.

The supercharger kit strategy reflects a growing market segment of truck owners who want genuine performance gains without the complexity or risk of third-party modifications. Factory-backed programs like Direct Connection offer the advantage of warranty consideration and technical support, making high-output upgrades more accessible to mainstream customers. The 900-horsepower threshold positions Ram competitively within the premium truck market, where performance credentials increasingly influence purchasing decisions.

title: Lucid Reveals New Cosmos Images, Says Sportier Gravity Coming Soon
summary: The Cosmos has a sloping roofline and could start production next year, while the hi-po Gravity is coming much sooner.
whatHappening: Lucid Motors has unveiled new images of its upcoming Cosmos model, revealing a sleek design with a sloping roofline. The company is also promising a high-performance variant of its Gravity SUV sooner than initially expected.
whoInvolved: Lucid Motors is an American EV manufacturer headquartered in Newark, California, which began producing the Lucid Air sedan in 2021 and started Gravity SUV production in December 2024. The company is now expanding its lineup with new models and performance variants.
whyMatters: The Cosmos and sportier Gravity represent Lucid's strategy to broaden its product range beyond the Air sedan and capture different market segments in the growing luxury EV space. Accelerating the high-performance Gravity's arrival could help Lucid compete more effectively against established luxury automakers while ramping up overall production volumes.
articleBody:
Lucid Motors is moving forward with its expansion plans, revealing new imagery of the upcoming Cosmos model while signaling that a more powerful version of its Gravity SUV will arrive ahead of schedule. According to Car and Driver, the Cosmos features a distinctive sloping roofline and could begin production as soon as next year, positioning it as another key addition to Lucid's growing electric vehicle lineup.

The Cosmos represents Lucid's third vehicle offering, following the Lucid Air sedan, which the company began manufacturing at its Casa Grande, Arizona factory in September 2021, and the Lucid Gravity SUV, which launched production in December 2024. The mid-size luxury crossover Gravity has already established itself as the brand's first SUV and second vehicle overall, arriving with a multitude of features and amenities aimed at the premium market segment.

The high-performance variant of the Gravity is particularly notable given its accelerated timeline. By bringing the sportier iteration to market sooner than previously announced, Lucid aims to offer customers a more dynamic option within its SUV portfolio while capitalizing on growing consumer interest in performance-oriented electric vehicles. This move suggests the company is confident in its production capabilities and supply chain as it scales manufacturing operations.

Lucid's portfolio expansion comes as the company continues to establish itself as both a direct automaker and a technology supplier. Beyond manufacturing its own vehicles, Lucid supplies advanced electric vehicle powertrain systems to other automakers, including Aston Martin, diversifying its revenue streams and leveraging its engineering expertise across the industry.

The introduction of the Cosmos adds another dimension to Lucid's strategy, targeting customers who may seek a different design language or market positioning than the Air or Gravity. With potential production starting next year, the timeline suggests the company has finalized development and is preparing manufacturing infrastructure to support the new model.

As Lucid navigates an increasingly competitive luxury EV market, the combination of new model launches and accelerated high-performance variants underscores the company's commitment to offering diverse options within its growing product family.

title: 2027 Kia Telluride X-Pro Test: Future-Proofed
summary: How compromised is the off-roadiest Telluride?
whatHappening: Car and Driver has tested the 2027 Kia Telluride X-Pro, the automaker's most off-road-capable variant of its three-row crossover SUV. The review examines how much capability Kia has engineered into the model and where it may have compromised practicality or on-road performance.
whoInvolved: Kia Corporation, South Korea's second-largest automobile manufacturer, is behind the Telluride line. The vehicle itself is a mid-size crossover SUV with three-row seating that Kia has produced since 2019, competing in one of the market's most popular segments.
whyMatters: The X-Pro variant signals Kia's push to capture buyers interested in both family hauling and light off-road capability—a growing market segment. The test results will influence perceptions of whether Kia's premium crossover can deliver genuine terrain prowess without sacrificing the comfort and utility that drive mainstream crossover sales.
articleBody:
Kia is making another bid for adventure-minded families with the 2027 Telluride X-Pro, its most rugged interpretation yet of the popular mid-size crossover. The X-Pro trim represents the automaker's effort to inject genuine off-road credibility into a platform best known for three-row seating and family-friendly features. According to Car and Driver, the central question driving the test was how far Kia could push the Telluride's off-road credentials without compromising the on-road refinement and practicality that have made the model a staple since its 2019 debut.

The Telluride itself has evolved into a cornerstone of Kia's global lineup. Since launching over five years ago, the crossover has captured significant market share in the three-row segment, appealing to buyers seeking a balance of space, comfort, and value. The X-Pro variant builds on that foundation by introducing enhancements aimed at rough terrain: upgraded suspension geometry, skid protection, all-terrain tires, and increased ground clearance. The model's positioning suggests Kia sees an opportunity to compete with slightly more rugged competitors while keeping the vehicle accessible to mainstream buyers.

Kia Corporation, headquartered in Seoul, has been aggressive in diversifying its model range and pushing upmarket in recent years. As South Korea's second-largest automaker after its parent company Hyundai Motor Company, Kia has the engineering resources and global distribution to test markets that rivals might avoid. The X-Pro variant of the Telluride represents a calculated bet that customers in key markets will embrace a crossover that can handle both school runs and weekend off-road excursions.

The test itself probes a fundamental tension in modern vehicle design: how much off-road performance can engineers layer onto a platform optimized for everyday comfort without introducing penalties in fuel economy, cargo space, or ride quality. Adding skid plates, all-terrain rubber, and suspension reinforcement increases weight and complexity. The challenge for Kia was ensuring those additions enhance capability without turning the Telluride into a vehicle that feels over-engineered for the mild off-roading most owners will actually attempt.

Results from this kind of hands-on assessment matter because they shape buyer confidence in a brand's claims. If the X-Pro delivers genuine terrain-handling improvements without sacrificing the refinement that made the standard Telluride appealing, it could broaden the crossover's appeal. Conversely, if compromises prove too severe, the variant risks alienating both mainstream buyers and serious off-road enthusiasts. The outcome will likely influence Kia's next steps in its adventure-focused product strategy.

title: The 2027 Polaris RZR Pro R Boost Is the Most Powerful Side-by-Side
summary: In the world of side-by-sides, no amount of horsepower is ever enough.
whatHappening: Polaris has unveiled the 2027 RZR Pro R Boost, a new side-by-side vehicle that sets a new power benchmark for the recreational off-road market. The latest iteration pushes horsepower to previously unseen levels in its class.
whoInvolved: Polaris Inc., an American automotive manufacturer headquartered in Medina, Minnesota, is releasing this vehicle. The company, which has engineered and manufactured vehicles in Roseau, Minnesota since its founding there, has a long history of producing recreational powersports vehicles beyond its well-known motorcycle brands.
whyMatters: The 2027 RZR Pro R Boost signals that manufacturers continue to escalate performance specs in the competitive side-by-side segment, where power output has become a key differentiator. For enthusiasts and buyers in this market, the vehicle represents the current pinnacle of what the category can deliver in terms of raw capability.
articleBody:
Polaris has announced the 2027 RZR Pro R Boost, the latest addition to its side-by-side vehicle lineup and a machine engineered to claim the title of most powerful in its class. According to Car and Driver, the powersports industry shows no signs of moderating horsepower ambitions, with manufacturers locked in an ongoing competition to deliver maximum performance.

The RZR Pro R Boost builds on Polaris's long track record in the recreational off-road vehicle market. Polaris Inc., headquartered in Medina, Minnesota, has maintained engineering and manufacturing operations in Roseau, Minnesota since the company's founding there, allowing the firm to develop and refine vehicles tailored to off-road enthusiasts. The RZR Pro R line has been a flagship offering within the broader side-by-side category, and this newest generation pushes the envelope further.

Side-by-side vehicles, also known as utility terrain vehicles or UTVs, have evolved dramatically over the past two decades from bare-bones utility machines into high-performance recreational platforms. The 2027 model year intensifies this trend by focusing on what many buyers in this segment prioritize: maximum engine output and acceleration capability.

The decision to boost the Pro R's power reflects market demand from a customer base that views horsepower as a core value proposition. Owners in this category often use their vehicles for both recreational trail riding and competitive events, where performance advantages translate directly into capability and bragging rights.

Polaris faces competition from other major powersports manufacturers in the side-by-side space, yet the company continues to invest in pushing performance boundaries. The 2027 RZR Pro R Boost represents a continuation of this strategy, targeting buyers who view their vehicles as premium, high-powered machines rather than basic utility tools.
